hero: Single-column, left-aligned opening screen with almost no ornament. Name 'Emil Kowalski' set as a plain heading immediately followed by the role 'Design Engineer', then one or two sentences of prose ('I like to build things for designers and developers... how it looks, feels, and behaves'). Credibility in the first 5 seconds comes not from a big visual but from name-dropping affiliations in copy (Linear, ex-Vercel) and from the restraint itself — the page performs taste by refusing a hero image, gradient, or animation. A single announcement/CTA line (e.g. 'Enrollment for my animation course is open') sits near the top as the only bit of color/urgency.
wordmark_identity: No graphic logo or monogram. Identity is the plain-text name set in the body UI sans at a modest size — deliberately un-branded. The 'ownable' identity is behavioral (motion quality) rather than a mark. There is no kinetic or variable-type wordmark; the name is static. Lesson for ECG-as-ligature: Emil proves you can skip a graphic identity entirely if the craft carries the brand, but that also means he has no reusable glyph — the ECG idea would give a distinctiveness he intentionally forgoes.
signature_detail: The signature is invisible/behavioral: sub-perceptual motion craft applied only where it earns its place. Concretely — micro-interactions built on transform + opacity, durations kept under ~300ms, spring/ease tuned so transitions feel physical not decorative, and a documented rule that high-frequency (keyboard-repeated) actions get NO animation at all. His component work (Sonner toasts, Vaul drawer) is the physical embodiment of the signature: a toast stack that settles, a drawer that drags with velocity. Used with restraint because the whole thesis is 'sometimes the best animation is no animation.' The ownable element is a felt sense of quality, not a visible glyph.
typography: UI is a clean grotesque sans (Inter/Geist-adjacent [uncertain]) with an understated hierarchy — section labels ('Projects', 'Writing', 'Newsletter', 'More') use consistent modest sizing rather than dramatic scale jumps, so contrast comes from weight and whitespace, not size. Article/prose pages widen to a generous single measure for comfortable reading and read as editorial [uncertain: possible serif body on longform]. No Fraunces-style display serif on the index; the type is quiet on purpose. Tracking is near-default; no showy optical-size play.
whitespace_layout: Vertical rhythm is the main design tool: one narrow centered/left-aligned reading column, sections separated by large consistent vertical gaps, no cards, no grid columns. Reading width is constrained (~600-700px feel) even on wide screens so the eye never has to hunt. 'Designed not templated' is achieved through disciplined spacing, precise line-height, and refusal of decoration rather than through unique layout shapes — it looks bespoke because everything is calm and consistent.
color_accent_discipline: Effectively monochromatic — near-black text on near-white (and inverse in dark). Accent color usage is minimal to nonexistent; any color is reserved for a single link/CTA state [uncertain on exact hue]. Accent occupies well under a few percent of the visual field. The restraint is the point: color is a rare event, so a link or the course CTA reads as the loudest thing on an otherwise neutral page.
light_dark_tone: Supports light and dark modes with a neutral grayscale tone system rather than a branded accent that must survive both. Because there's essentially no saturated brand color, theme switching is trivial and never breaks. The dark mode is calm (soft off-black, not pure #000) so long-form reading stays comfortable [uncertain on exact tokens].
motion: Entrance motion is subtle and opacity/transform-only; nothing slides in with long durations. Timings held under ~300ms (he cites 180ms as snappy vs 400ms as sluggish). Easing is hand-tuned spring/custom-cubic for a physical feel. Scroll behavior is quiet — no parallax spectacle. Hover states are small and immediate. The governing discipline: animate only to explain functionality, add responsiveness, maintain spatial continuity, or delight in RARE interactions; never animate high-frequency/keyboard actions. Motion is a scalpel, applied to few elements, tuned obsessively.
reduced_motion_a11y: Reduced-motion discipline is effectively the site's thesis — his writing explicitly argues large classes of UI should not animate at all, which is stronger than a prefers-reduced-motion fallback. Site almost certainly honors prefers-reduced-motion [uncertain on exact implementation], but the deeper lesson is designing so the no-motion state is already the correct baseline experience, with motion as pure enhancement. Keyboard/focus and contrast are respected given the clinical simplicity, though specific ARIA/focus specifics unverified [uncertain].
project_presentation: Projects shown as a dense, scannable LIST — each row is a title + one-line description + link (e.g. 'Sonner — An opinionated toast component for React', 'Vaul — a drawer component for React', 'animations.dev', 'index.how'). No screenshots, cards, or case-study pages on the index; the artifact IS the shipped component, so the 'demo' is that you can go use the real library. Deep-dive density is deferred to separate long-form 'How I built...' articles rather than crammed into the index. High signal-to-noise: he trusts the reader to know Sonner/Vaul.
research_artifact_presentation: No academic-paper or publication apparatus — there are no citations, PDFs, or venue metadata. The equivalent of 'research artifacts' here is his writing/education output (course, essays) and open-source libraries, presented as plain titled links. Relevant lesson: even a technical author can skip formal citation chrome entirely if the work links to canonical live artifacts (GitHub repos, npm packages, course site). [uncertain: no dedicated publications section observed]
writing_blog_integration: Writing is fused directly into the home page as a first-class section, not siloed on a separate blog domain — the index lists ~9 essays inline as titled links ('You Don't Need Animations', 'Developing Taste', '7 Practical Animation Tips', 'Great animations', 'Dynamic Island', 'How I built my course platform'). Work and writing coexist in the same vertical scroll, signaling that thinking is part of the portfolio. Feed is low-density (titles only, no excerpts/thumbnails on index). Likely MDX/Next.js content [uncertain on CMS].
photography_imagery: Essentially no personal photography or lifestyle imagery — the site is text and shipped UI. Any imagery is functional (interactive animation demos embedded inside articles, product screenshots inside case studies) rather than personal media. Lesson: media earns its place only when it demonstrates the craft; there is no 'me at the beach' section competing with the technical work.
navigation: No persistent top nav bar in the traditional sense — navigation is the vertical section flow of the single page (intro -> Projects -> Writing -> Newsletter -> More). The name/wordmark sits at the top of the page, not stickied. External links (Twitter, GitHub) grouped last under a 'More' heading. Order front-loads work and writing; social/contact deprioritized to the bottom.
trust_credibility: Credibility surfaced through copy and recognizable artifacts rather than a logo wall — mentions of Linear (current) and Vercel (past) live in the intro prose, and trust is carried by name-recognition of his open-source (Sonner/Vaul are widely used in the React ecosystem). No testimonials, client logos, or badges cluttering the hero; the shipped work is the proof.
contact_conversion: Primary conversion is the newsletter signup ('Exclusive, newsletter-only content once a month. No spam, no nonsense') plus the paid animation course as the commercial CTA. Contact is low-friction and indirect — social links (Twitter/GitHub) under 'More' rather than a form or Cal.com booking. The funnel favors audience-building (email) over one-off contact.
performance_weight: Very light page — mostly text, system-adjacent variable sans, minimal JS on the index, no hero video or large imagery, so it feels instant. Built on Next.js/React. Font loading is likely a single variable sans with fast swap [uncertain on exact strategy]. Performance is treated as a design constraint: the restraint that defines the aesthetic also keeps weight and Core Web Vitals excellent almost for free.
takeaway: STEAL: the discipline of making the no-motion / no-color baseline already correct, then adding motion only as a rare, sub-300ms transform/opacity enhancement — perfect model for an ECG animation that must degrade gracefully and read as clinical-credible under prefers-reduced-motion. Also steal the fused writing-in-portfolio single scroll and the list-not-cards project density. AVOID: his total absence of a graphic identity and accent color — for the Madhavi brand (editorial-minimal, maroon, ECG signature) going as monochrome/anonymous as Emil would waste the ownable ECG-as-ligature and maroon accent; keep his restraint but spend it deliberately on one signature, not zero.
